# sentinels

> sentinels is open-source (MIT) host intrusion detection and response for Linux, macOS and Windows. Its agent, `garrett`, is one program file. It ends a break-in while it is still starting, cleans up after it and explains why in plain sentences. The optional fleet service runs on the owner's own hardware.

Key facts:

- Install on Linux and macOS: `curl -fsSL https://gary23w.github.io/sentinels/install.sh | sudo sh`
- Install on Windows, from an elevated PowerShell: `irm https://gary23w.github.io/sentinels/install.ps1 | iex`
- Response modes: `kill` (the default) ends a hostile program and everything it started; `pause` freezes it for an operator; `decide` freezes it and lets the service's configured model decide; `report` only reports.
- The default `kill` mode does not call a model. AI case analysis and `decide` mode need a provider configured on the service.
- No account, cloud console or kernel module is needed. Installed by itself, the agent keeps its cases on the machine.
- `garrett restore <case>` puts back what was cleaned up after a stop; `garrett trust <case>` marks a program as the owner's.
- It knows the marks an automated or AI operator leaves under a web server or a document program: many different commands at machine pace, retries with small changes, and the same command started in parallel.

## Docs

- [sentinels(8)](https://gary23w.github.io/sentinels/): install, response modes, apt repository, fleet service, updates
- [garrett(8) manual](https://gary23w.github.io/sentinels/manual.html): every command, the configuration file, learning, the privacy shield, firmware and boot checks, network checks, updates
- [AI-operated intrusions](https://gary23w.github.io/sentinels/ai-attacks.html): what an intrusion run by an AI agent looks like on a host and how garrett ends it
